methodology.scope: Revised rubric: useful quality and efficiency, not smallest file or shortest run. The ten category weights total 100. Current records support five visual judgments (65% of the intended rubric), but not a complete efficiency score. The visible ranking is visual-only.
methodology.formula: Visual score = round(100 × earned visual points / 65). A complete overall score is sum(score / 10 × weight), rounded, ONLY when all ten categories have comparable evidence. Unknown categories remain null; they are neither zero nor neutral points.
methodology.unknownPolicy: No placeholder ratings. Missing verified accepted distance, complete timing, human labor or controlled performance prevents a full quality-and-efficiency total. Five visual categories are currently assessed; the other five say Not scored. The old combined rankings are withdrawn, not directly comparable with these visual-only scores.
comparisonLimits: Cost must be divided by unique useful coverage at a common quality target. Source seconds, photos and raw camera counts do not prove coverage: a car may stop, drive faster, repeat a road or extract multiple lens views at one position.

Accepted corridor metres count a street section once, even with two directions, two lenses or repeated passes. Measure the road and both facade bands separately and count only sections meeting the agreed view/detail requirement. Do not divide bytes by a subjective quality score.

No current record supplies verified metric scale plus a measured accepted street length. Metre-normalized size and time are therefore unknown, not guessed from SfM units or an arbitrary driving speed.

Same-capture comparisons can show delivered MB and training-stage costs for equal input extent. They still do not prove equal successful coverage, equal quality, end-to-end cost or a more efficient usable street.

Visual scores remain editorial judgments backed by examples. Different camera routes, scene complexity and capture conditions limit cross-capture ranking; prefer matched views to infer method effects.
The browser cost proxy and evidence-quality bonus were removed. Splat count, records and confidence stay as facts; they no longer add points for quality or performance.
The 8 fps review clips cannot establish live frame pacing or high-frequency flicker. Real-time runtime and startup need dedicated controlled measurements; physical-phone behavior is unmeasured.
Packaging remains part of delivery cost. Compare equivalent exported quality/SH/LOD and unique usable extent; report PLY/SOG differences rather than attributing all savings to training.
methodology.previewProtocol: Each model has a 960×540, 75° field-of-view, 80-frame review encoded at 8 fps: 0–6s along the route, 6–10s lateral. Review duration is not capture duration. Eight labelled samples plus 1:1 center crops support the written observations. No enhancement was applied. Review paths match within the original-turn, A/B, construction and residential review groups; MRNF is a separate review path; original-turn/MRNF lateral offsets are arbitrary reconstruction units, not measured lane widths. Compressed previews and sparse sampling cannot measure high-frequency flicker or live performance.
methodology.coverageExample: Example only: 1,000 usable metres at 500 MB = 50 MB/100 m. 500 usable metres at 200 MB = 40 MB/100 m: 20% less storage per equal length, or 25% more length per MB. Equal required quality and viewpoint coverage are prerequisites.
acceptanceProtocol: Define the required street section and supported driving corridor before comparing: both sides, forward views and lateral offsets, with the same displayed resolution.

Obtain a metric reference from validated map/GNSS/control measurements; retain scale uncertainty. Overlay the reconstructed coverage on that reference instead of treating arbitrary camera units as metres.

Review identical route and lateral checkpoints. Mark each road/left-facade/right-facade interval pass, fail or unreviewed for legibility, stable surfaces, holes and ghosts. Freeze these acceptance criteria before evaluating variants.
Take the union of accepted physical intervals. Repeated captures and opposite-direction views improve support but do not double the street length. Unreviewed intervals earn no accepted length.

Report accepted metres and acceptance fraction with MB/100 m, full processing minutes/100 m and human minutes/100 m. Zero accepted length means no usable efficiency result, never an infinitely good score.

Keep raw data facts alongside the result: input frames, source intervals, registered cameras, source/processed bytes, training time, export format and splat count. They explain cost without pretending to measure usable coverage.
